newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma says Suu Kyi "poisoned" by foreign awards.
newsitem.headline: Burma says Suu Kyi "poisoned" by foreign awards.

text.p: Burma's official media said on Tuesday that pro-democracy leader Aung San Suu Kyi was being poisoned by the awards conferred upon her by other countries.
"The awards being conferred on Daw Aung San Suu Kyi today from outside the country are in fact poisons," said the commentary published in both Burmese-language newspapers.
State-run newspapers are considered the mouthpiece of the military government.
"Do you realise that poisons are being poured into your head in order to make you hate the government, the armed forces and the people of Myanmar (Burma) more and more?" the commentary asked.

Suu Kyi, winner of the 1991 Nobel Peace Prize for her non-violent campaign for democracy, has been awarded dozens of honours and awards abroad over the past few years for her efforts to bring democracy back to Burma.
She has not accepted any of them in person, as she fears she will not be allowed to return to the country if she leaves.
On Sunday she was given an honorary doctorate of law from American University in Washington D.C.

Suu Kyi's husband, British academic Michael Aris, accepted the award in her place and delivered a message from Suu Kyi urging students to discourage corporate America from doing business with the military rulers.
The newspaper commentary chastised Suu Kyi for her attacks on Burma.
"What are you doing for the national cause of Myanmar (Burma)?" it asked. "You are only doing this to hinder and destruct the development of national interests," it said.
"Never forget till your last breath that the SLORC government is Myanmar's national government."
The State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) seized power in 1988 after crushing pro-democracy street demonstrations, leaving thousands dead or in jail.
The SLORC placed Suu Kyi under house arrest in 1989 for her attacks on the military government. She was released in July, 1995.
Suu Kyi's National League for Democracy (NLD) party won a landslide victory in a 1990 general election, but the SLORC refused to recognise the result.
